To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) trust management is equivalent to access control lists, 2) unforgeable references are a proper subset of access control lists, which in turn is equivalent to capabilities, and 3) trust management is a tractable compromise that lies between access control lists and capabilities.
the trust management access control mechanism is a tractable compromise, and that it is equivalent to a form of capabilities.

(1) access control lists are more expressive and flexible than capability systems, (2) trust management provides an efficient compromise between access control lists and capabilities, and (3) the access control mechanisms at the heart of trust management systems can be viewed as a combination of access control lists and a form of capabilities that is more expressive than capabilities viewed as rows in the access matrix.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formal analysis of the core access control mechanism of trust management systems.
the fundamental access control mechanism of a variety of distributed trust management and authorization systems.
the analysis of trust management systems and the comparison of trust management with other access control mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the access control mechanism of trust management is more expressive than the access control mechanisms of capabilities, access control lists and role-based access control, but less expressive than the access matrix.
the access control mechanism in trust management systems is the only one that provides a reasonable compromise between unrestricted capability-passing and easy revocation.
access control lists, capabilities, and trust management systems are equivalent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the trust management approach to access control can be understood as a hybrid between capabilities and access control lists, with a more tractable compromise between the advantages and disadvantages of each.
trust management is a tractable compromise that is more powerful than capabilities, but less than access control lists.
trust management is a natural extension of capabilities, which in turn is a natural extension (in terms of expressiveness) of access control lists.
The main takeaway from our work is that
trust management systems provide a natural and useful compromise between the flexibility of capability systems and the ease of revocation provided by ACLs.
trust management, as a mechanism for access control, is a natural extension of capabilities that provides a tractable compromise with the revocation features of access control lists.
trust management is a natural extension of the capability model that is more expressive and tractable, and is a more natural model for access control than access control lists.
